stem: While comparing federal and state law, a Valium prescription with unused refills was issued seven months ago. Which clock controls?

choices.text: Dispense because unused authorized refills survive for one year if its alternate trigger can be documented.
Use the date of the last refill to start a new six-month period.
Renew the prescription based solely on the patient's request.
The prescription may not be refilled more than six months after issue.
Transfer it and apply a new issue date at the receiving pharmacy.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'The prescription may not be refilled more than six months after issue.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Dispense because unused authorized refills survive for one year.' would require that Schedule IV prescriptions had a one-year refill window. The decisive cue appears in 'While comparing federal and state law, a Valium prescription with unused refills was issued seven months ago. Which clock controls?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Dispense because unused authorized refills survive for one year.' would apply only if Schedule IV prescriptions had a one-year refill window; 'While comparing federal and state law, a Valium prescription with unused refills was issued seven months ago. Which clock controls?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Use the date of the last refill to start a new six-month period.' would apply only if federal timing ran from last dispensing rather than issue; 'While comparing federal and state law, a Valium prescription with unused refills was issued seven months ago. Which clock controls?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Renew the prescription based solely on the patient's request.' would apply only if the pharmacist could supply practitioner renewal authority; 'While comparing federal and state law, a Valium prescription with unused refills was issued seven months ago. Which clock controls?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'The prescription may not be refilled more than six months after issue.': supported by schedule iii-iv refills.
choice_analysis.E: 'Transfer it and apply a new issue date at the receiving pharmacy.' would apply only if transfer altered the original issue date; 'While comparing federal and state law, a Valium prescription with unused refills was issued seven months ago. Which clock controls?' states otherwise.

related_facts: diazepam (Valium) is used for anxiety disorders, acute alcohol withdrawal, muscle spasm, and adjunctive seizure treatment; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
